newsitem.title: UK: Algeria heads Middle East rights abuses-Amnesty.
newsitem.headline: Algeria heads Middle East rights abuses-Amnesty.

text.p: Amnesty International on Wednesday highlighted Algeria's poor human rights record and said unfair trials, torture and executions were carried out in most countries in the Middle East and North Africa.

However, in its annual report, the London-based group said a number of positive steps had occurred, among them Kuwait ratifying a UN convention against torture and Morocco/Western Sahara releasing six prisoners of conscience.
Algeria was guilty of all major human rights abuses and Amnesty said thousands of people were killed and executed by both government security forces and opposition groups in 1996.
Torture of detainees continued to be widespread, hundreds of death sentences were imposed and hundreds of people arrested by the security forces remain unaccounted for, Amnesty said.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria since 1992 when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the radical Islamic Salvation Front took a huge lead.
There was a significant rise in the number of executions in many countries in the region and the use of torture was widely recorded in almost every country in the Middle East.
In Iran, at least 110 people were executed, more than twice the level in 1995, while in Iraq hundreds of people, including army officers and political prisoners, were executed.
At least 69 people were executed in Saudi Arabia.
In Iraq, torture of detainees remained widespread and serious human rights abuses were carried out in Kurdish-controlled provinces by Kurdish groups.

Under the jurisdiction of the Palestinian Authority, at least 18 people received "grossly unfair" trials while in Israel and the occupied territories at least 600 Palestinians received unfair trials, Amnesty said.
